texts.preamble: Chaggan Lal vs State (2025:Rj-Jd:4931) on 22 January, 2025 Author: Kuldeep Mathur Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2025:Rj-Jd:4931] High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 1145/2007 Chaggan Lal S/o Ota Ram Ji, R/o Sindrath, Tehsil & Distt. Sirohi ----Petitioner Versus The State of Rajasthan through Pp ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. S.K. Verma For Respondent(s) : Mr. Urja Ram Kalbi, Pp Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Kuldeep Mathur Order 22/01/2025 By way of filing the present revision petition under Section 397 read with Section 401 Cr.P.C., the petitioner-accused has challenged the order/judgment dated 14.06.2007 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sirohi, in Criminal Case No.330/01 whereby he has been convicted for the offence under section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo one year's S.I. and a fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further
texts.facts: As per prosecution, on 10.03.2000, the Food Inspector collected milk samples from the petitioner who is a milk vendor. The same were sent for examination to the Public Analyst, Jodhpur after duly following the procedure provided under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The Public Analyst in its report found that the milk samples to be 'Adulterated'. During the course of trial, the prosecution examined as many as 5 witnesses and several documents were also exhibited. Learned counsel submitted that the sentence awarder to the petitioner has already been suspended by this Court vide order dated 11.10.2007 passed in S.B. Cr. Misc. (Suspension of Sentence) Application No.303/2007. Chaggan Lal vs State (2025:Rj-Jd:4931) on 22 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24396798/ 1
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents. He further submitted that the incident in the present case occurred in the year 2000. There is no positive evidence regarding mixing of water in the milk by the petitioner and in absence thereof, only on the basis of the report of Public Analyst, it cannot be said that the petitioner had committed the alleged crime or the milk was adulterated. Learned counsel for the petitioner in the alternative submitted that since the occurrence relates to year 2000 and the petitioner has already served some part of the sentence awarded to him, therefore the substantive sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him. Reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka: 2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623 and a judgment of Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CriLJ 2582.

State of Rajasthan: 2014 CriLJ 2582.
